issues.legal_issue: A person who was already in possession before premises became public premises is not in unauthorised occupation merely by continuing in possession, and an eviction notice under the public-premises statute cannot be issued on that basis.
material_facts: The occupants were in possession of the property before it was sold to the government and thereby became public premises.
The occupants remained in possession when an eviction notice was issued under the public-premises statute.
The government did not claim that the occupants first entered into possession after the sale.
The occupants were not government allottees, lessees or grantees whose entitlement had been determined or cancelled.
issues.conclusion: The occupants were not in unauthorised occupation under section 3, so the Collector lacked jurisdiction to issue the eviction notice under section 4(1); the notice was quashed and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3(a), the words “entered into possession thereof” require entry into possession of premises that are already public premises; prior possession does not become unauthorised merely because the premises later become public. Section 3(b) applies to an allottee, lessee or grantee from the government whose entitlement ends by determination or cancellation, and section 3(c) did not apply. Under section 4(1), the Collector may issue an eviction notice only where the person is in unauthorised occupation. No earlier case was relied on in deciding this issue.

rule.if: public_premises_eviction_proceeding and possession_began_before_public_status and not government_entitlement_terminated

predicates.public_premises_eviction_proceeding: An authority initiates a statutory proceeding to evict a person from premises treated as public premises.
predicates.possession_began_before_public_status: The person was already in possession before the premises became public premises.
predicates.government_entitlement_terminated: The person occupied under a government allotment, lease or grant that was later determined or cancelled.

issues.definition: When a statutory public-premises eviction proceeding concerns a person whose possession began before the premises became public and who has no terminated government entitlement, the eviction notice lacks jurisdiction.
